title: pseudognaphalium roseum
intro: Pseudognaphalium roseum, commonly known as Rose cudweed, is a type of flowering plant in the daisy family (Asteraceae). Rose cudweed is used in herbal medicine for its numerous health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may help to soothe wounds, reduce fever, and protect against cell damage. The plant's therapeutic actions include its ability to modulate the immune system, reduce inflammation, and exhibit antimicrobial activity, making it a potential treatment for various conditions such as skin infections and respiratory issues. The bioactive constituents of Pseudognaphalium roseum include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
